chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Ibn Sinan from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a muqatib (a slave who has agreed to pay a sum for his freedom) who dies having paid part of his manumission price, and he has a son by his concubine: He (the Imam) said, if it was stipulated that if he becomes unable [to pay], he returns to slavery, then his son returns to slavery along with the concubine. And if it was not stipulated, his son pays what remains of the manumission price and inherits what remains [of the estate].

key_terms.جَارِيَتِهِ: His concubine (female slave with whom he has relations)
key_terms.عَجَزَ: Became unable (to pay the remaining debt)
key_terms.مُكَاتَبٍ: A slave who has contracted with his master to pay a specific sum for his freedom
key_terms.مُكَاتَبَتِهِ: The manumission price or contract of freedom

ai.seo_question: What happens to the son and estate of a slave who dies during his manumission contract?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal status of a mukatab's family upon his death, emphasizing that the default clause determines whether the son and concubine revert to slavery or remain free. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that contractual stipulations govern the transition of status, ensuring the son can either settle the debt to secure his freedom or inherit the remaining estate. The narration underscores the importance of precise contract terms in determining the financial and social standing of the deceased's dependents.
